explanation: Public displays of affection like kissing or prolonged hugging are tolerated in big cities and tourist resorts but can draw unwanted stares, and are more frowned upon in conservative or rural areas. Social attitudes toward public affection, especially among same-sex couples, remain notably more conservative outside secular, educated, urban circles.
local_tip: Keep public affection light (hand-holding is fine) and save more visible affection for private settings, especially outside major cities.
regional_note: Istanbul, Izmir, and tourist resorts are considerably more tolerant than rural or conservative inland regions.

also_check.note: PDA is strictly discouraged and can draw legal trouble, even for married couples.
Cheek-kissing as a greeting and light PDA are common and socially accepted.
Public affection is seen as embarrassing and generally avoided, though attitudes are slowly shifting among younger people.
